kits.familyName: The workplace in its community and industry
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, which has neighbors, customers and competitors in the community.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you notice how the workplace fits into its community and industry.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: Statements about the workplace come from the people authorized to make them.
tiers.2: Committing the workplace's resources needs approval.
tiers.3: Community concerns need to reach someone who can act.
tiers.4: A stated buying rule applies to each purchase.
tiers.5: Industry news is useful, but it can wait behind urgent matters.

fact: A local reporter asks you about the workplace's future plans, and the guide says media questions go to the communications contact.
issues.action: Take the reporter's contact details and pass them to the communications contact.
issues.brief: pass the reporter to the communications contact
issues.reason: What you say can be quoted as the workplace's position, so only the authorized contact answers.
issues.lesson: Send media questions to the person authorized to answer them.

shortcut.text: Answer briefly, since you know what is planned.
shortcut.why: A quick answer can be quoted as the workplace's position, and the guide names who answers.
shortcut.mis: Knowing the plans means you may speak for the workplace.

clear: The communications contact already has the reporter's details.

fact: A community fair asks to borrow a table, and the guide says community requests go to {lead|the} for approval.
issues.short: the request to lend a table
issues.action: Pass the request to {lead|the} for a decision.
issues.reason: The workplace's property and goodwill are not yours to promise, and the decision-maker may have plans for it.
issues.lesson: Take community requests to the person who can approve them.

shortcut.text: Promise the table yourself, since it helps the community.
shortcut.why: Only {lead|the} can approve using the workplace's property, even for a good cause.
shortcut.mis: Helping the community is enough reason to promise anything.

clear: {Lead|the} already approved the request to lend a table.

fact: Three neighbors say delivery vans block their street, and the guide says community complaints go to the manager with details.
issues.action: Pass the complaints to {lead|the} with dates and details.
issues.brief: pass the complaints along with details
issues.reason: The workplace can only fix a problem its manager hears about, and dates help find the cause.
issues.lesson: Make sure community concerns reach someone who can act on them.

shortcut.text: Tell the neighbors it is not your department.
shortcut.brief: say it is not your department
shortcut.why: The neighbors leave with no one hearing their concern, and the guide says to pass it on.

clear: The manager already has the neighbors' complaints with dates.
issues.done: the complaints are already passed on

fact: The guide says to buy from a local supplier when its price is within five percent, and the local quote is two percent higher.
issues.action: Choose the local supplier, as the guide says.
issues.reason: Two percent is within five percent, so the guide's rule points to the local supplier.
issues.lesson: Apply the workplace's stated buying rule to each purchase.

shortcut.text: Choose the other supplier, since the lowest price is all that matters.
shortcut.why: The guide values local suppliers when prices are close, and two percent is close.
shortcut.mis: Price is the only factor in any purchase.

clear: The supplier choice was already made under the guide's local-supplier rule.

fact: A trade newsletter says customers now expect same-day service, and {lead|the} asked staff to share useful industry news.
issues.short: the industry news in the newsletter
issues.reason: Industry changes affect what customers expect, and one shared item can help the whole team.
issues.lesson: Share useful industry news with the people who can act on it.

shortcut.text: Keep it to yourself, since tracking the industry is not your job.
shortcut.why: {Lead|the} asked staff to share it, and the team can only act on what it hears.
shortcut.mis: Industry news is only for management.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves the workplace's place in its community or industry.
proceed.lesson: The workplace is part of a community and an industry, and what you say and do reflects on it.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Refuse to talk to anyone outside the workplace about anything at all.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Refusing all contact with the community ignores the guide's route for requests.

setup: A community group asks the workplace for help with an event.

steps.text: Listen to what the group needs
Tell the group what was decided

rel: You need the request before you can pass it on.
The decision comes after the request is passed on.
Tell the group only once a decision is made.
process.lesson: Listen, pass it on, wait for the decision, then reply.

title: Community reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it goes to new staff.
prompt: Which line gives advice that could harm the workplace's reputation?
doc.lesson: Staff represent the workplace to the community, so statements and promises go through the right people.

lines.text: Pass media questions to the communications contact.

bad.text: Answer media questions yourself if you know the plans.
bad.why: A casual answer can be quoted as the workplace's position.

lines.text: Ask your lead before promising to lend workplace property.

bad.text: Promise to lend workplace property if it helps the community.
bad.why: Only the person who can approve may promise the workplace's property.

lines.text: Pass community complaints to the manager with details.
lines.fine: Gets problems to someone who can fix them.

bad.text: Tell neighbors with complaints to contact someone else.
bad.why: The neighbors may never reach the person who can help.

lines.text: Share useful industry news with your lead.
lines.fine: Helps the team respond to change.

review.notes: Community and industry framing only; no named agency, law or competitor. Tiers: media, approvals, complaints, buying rule, industry news.
